The following problem needs to be amended, it's something Voat, Inc. could suffer, too:

You open a post. Read the top comment and think "[Haha! | That's what needed to be said, well done. | etc.] I'll upvote that." Read the comment(thread) below it. And maybe the next.

The problem: The comments at the top are dinosaurs. They are likely to appeal to many people so they get even more upvotes or at least few downvotes. The comments further down are read by less people.

This needn't be fatal if the audience is mostly proper, e.g. if they prefer the comment that says and proves "The post title is a damn lie." to be at the top instead of the really funny joke that everybody gets. But it's certainly a problem because it changes the vote score from meaning "Many consciously decided to upvote this." to something else.

I have no good idea how to amend this, though. One bad idea I have is to have no upvote arrows for the top 10% of the comments or something.

Users are slower to debate, and quicker to make jokes or impulsively agree with the first thing that sounds like it could be correct.

This is in large part about the up / down voting system, users value their imaginary points and learn over time how to appease the groupthink and score higher meaningless points.

If you want to see honest debate and opinion remove any effects of up / down votes and remove the ability of the users to see the up down votes themselves, so their comment may move up and down in the list via votes but there is no total points on their profile that they can view.

Might be prudent to remove up/down votes on comments entirely, solely use it as a feedback indicator on how welcome a given article or self post happens to be. At the very least, hide the scores from view.
